label: <DEL> delimiter step (more often for longer sequences)
explanation: Fires almost only on the <DEL> delimiter step (t == L): 98% of activation mass and 95% of activations sit there, and the top activations are all at <DEL>. It is active on only about 61% of delimiter steps, though. The firing rate goes up with sequence length (precision at the delimiter: 0.33 for L=3, 0.51 for L=5, 0.69 for L=7, 0.75 for L=9), and the strongest activations come at long sequences. Which delimiters fire also depends on the content of the original tokens: adding the condition that the sequence contains any of 1/c/j/t/v/n/k/f raises F1 only slightly, to 0.77, so this dependence is diffuse and I did not capture it. Weak spillover onto the first copy step (recall_idx 1, about 2% of steps, notably when that output is b or i) and onto rare original-phase steps. Essentially silent on original-phase and later copy steps.
